title: What time do you finish?
goal: Agree a time with Maryam, your colleague, to meet about work.
tip: To fix a time, say the day, then is-sāʿa and the hour. No word for 'at' is needed: bāchir is-sāʿa tisʿ w rubʿ (tomorrow at 9:15), baʿd bāchir iṣ-ṣubḥ (the day after tomorrow, in the morning).
grammar: Telling the time with a day: bāchir is-sāʿa tisʿ
dialogue: Salim, what time do you finish today?
khams w nuṣṣ. w inti mita bitkhallṣīn?
Half past five. And when do you finish?
أنا أخلص بدري. نتلاقى باكر الساعة تسع؟
ana akhalliṣ badri. nitlāga bāchir is-sāʿa tisʿ?
I finish early. Shall we meet tomorrow at nine?
Tomorrow I've got an appointment. The day after?
زين. بعد باكر الساعة تسع وربع يناسبك؟
zēn. baʿd bāchir is-sāʿa tisʿ w rubʿ ynāsbak?
OK. Does the day after tomorrow at quarter past nine suit you?
Yes, that suits me. It's a deal!
items: when will you finish? (to a man)
to a woman: mita bitkhallṣīn? (متى بتخلصين؟)
ana akhalliṣ is-sāʿa khams = I finish at five
does it suit you? (to a man)
ma ynāsibni = it doesn't suit me

title: Come on, quick!
goal: Hurry a friend out of the door: get up, look, listen, take it, come.
tip: To tell a man to do something, drop the t- of the 'you' verb: tshūf → shūf (look), trūḥ → rūḥ (go), tgūm → gūm (get up). Where two consonants would start the word, add i-: tismaʿ → ismaʿ (listen). 'Come' and 'take' have their own forms: taʿāl, khudh.
grammar: Imperative to a man: gūm, shūf, rūḥ, taʿāl
dialogue: No, look at the time! Come on, quick.
OK. Listen, where did I put my phone?
Over there. Take it and come!
items: my phone: tilifōni; you'll also hear mobāyl (موبايل)
to a woman: khudhi; khudhah = take it
to a woman: taʿāli; to a group: taʿālu

title: Wait a minute
goal: Ask Maryam to come and look at a problem at work, and follow her instructions.
tip: To a woman, add -i to the man's form: shūf → shūfi (look), taʿāl → taʿāli (come). In verbs like ṭarrish, the short i before the last consonant drops: ṭarrish-li → ṭarrshī-li (send me). 'Wait' (UAE) is trayya to a man, trayyi to a woman.
grammar: Imperative to a woman: add -i (taʿāli, shūfi)
dialogue: Maryam, come and have a look, please.
Send me the email and I'll have a look.
هيه، وصل. ييب لي الملف بعد
Yes, it's come. Bring me the file too.
items: to a woman: trayyi (تريي); you'll see written اتريا; Kuwait: inṭir (انطر); never istanna (استنى)
to a woman: yībī-li (ييبي لي); you'll see written جيب لي; ييب alone also means 'he brings'
what's up? what's the matter? (also: what's wrong with it?)
about a person: shfīk? (what's wrong with you?)

title: Come here, everyone!
goal: Call Saif and his friends together for a photo at Global Village: come, come closer, look, smile, let me, let's.
tip: To a group, add -u to the man's form: taʿāl → taʿālu, shūf → shūfu, garrib → garrbu (come closer; the i drops). Khalli means 'let': khallni ashūf (let me see), khallna nrūḥ (let's go); to a group, khallūni. The next verb has no 'to'.
grammar: Imperative to a group: add -u (taʿālu, shūfu); khallni
dialogue: Let me take your photo. Come a bit closer.
خلني أشوف. حلوة! يلا، خلنا نروح
khallni ashūf. ḥilwa! yalla, khallna nrūḥ
Let me see. Lovely! Come on, let's go.
items: to one man: taʿāl; to one woman: taʿāli
to a woman: khallīni (خليني); to a group: khallūni (خلوني); khallni ashūf = let me see
aṣawwrak = I'll take your photo (to a man); aṣawwirkum (to a group)
to one man: garrib; to one woman: garrbi
to one man: shūf; to one woman: shūfi
smile (for a photo; lit. laugh) (to a group)
to one man: iẓḥak; to one woman: iẓḥaki
culture: In public places, ask before you photograph people and keep women and families you don't know out of your photos. Many families prefer that photos of their women aren't taken or shared. (Needs a native check.)

title: Don't go yet
goal: Say goodbye to Saif at the end of the evening: don't go, don't forget, don't worry, take care.
tip: For 'don't', put la before the ordinary 'you' verb, not the command form: trūḥ → la trūḥ (don't go), tinsa → la tinsa (don't forget). To a woman the verb keeps -īn: la trūḥīn, la tḥātīn; to a group -ūn: la trūḥūn.
grammar: Don't: la + the 'you' verb (la trūḥ, la trūḥīn)
dialogue: I have to, I've got work tomorrow morning.
لا تحاتي، هذا هو. في أمان الله
la tḥāti, hādha huwa. fī amān illāh
Don't worry, here it is. Bye.
مع السلامة. انتبه، لا تسوق بسرعة!
maʿa s-salāma. intibih, la tsūg b-surʿa!
Bye. Take care, don't drive fast!
items: to a woman: la trūḥīn; to a group: la trūḥūn (لا تروحون)
ʿindi dawām = I'm working (I have work); also school or university hours
for a feminine thing: hādhi hiya
be careful, take care (to a man)
to a woman: la tsūgīn b-surʿa
culture: Evenings in the Gulf start late, especially in summer, when the day is too hot to go out. Friends often meet after the ʿisha prayer and stay out until midnight, so ten o'clock can still be taww in-nās.

title: Checkpoint: errands with Maryam
goal: Maryam pops out to the bank: ask her to bring something back, answer her reminder and talk about what you did.
tip: This checkpoint mixes requests with the past. To a woman the command adds -i (yībī-li, khudhi), and 'don't' keeps -īn (la tḥātīn, la tinsīn). The past: ṭarrashtah (I sent it).
dialogue: سالم، أنا رايحة البنك. برجع على طول
Sālim, ana rāyḥa l-bank. barjaʿ ʿala ṭūl
Salim, I'm going to the bank. I'll be straight back.
زين. ييبي لي قهوة، الله يخليج
OK. Bring me a coffee, please.
إن شاء الله. لا تنسى الإيميل!
in shāʼ allāh. la tinsa l-īmēl!
لا تحاتين، طرشته البارحة. خذي، عشرين درهم
la tḥātīn, ṭarrashtah il-bārḥa. khudhi, ʿishrīn dirham
Don't worry, I sent it yesterday. Here, take twenty dirhams.
زين. بس لا تنسين، بدون سكر!
zēn. bas la tinsīn, bidūn sukkar!
OK. But don't forget, no sugar!
items: to a man: yīb-li; you'll see written جيبي لي

title: Do you want to come?
goal: Invite Maryam to lunch, hear her say no, and offer to bring her something back.
tip: abi (I want) and tabi (you want) take the next verb straight after, with no word for 'to': abi atghadda (I want to have lunch), ma abi aṭlaʿ (I don't want to go out). To a woman both verbs take -īn: tabīn trūḥīn? (do you want to go?)
grammar: Want + verb: abi atghadda, tabi trūḥ, tabīn trūḥīn
dialogue: Maryam, do you want to come with us?
The mall. I want to have lunch there.
مشكور، بس ما أبي أطلع. عندي شغل
mashkūr, bas ma abi aṭlaʿ. ʿindi shughul
Thanks, but I'd rather not go out. I've got work.
No problem. Do you want me to bring you anything?
هيه، أي شي حلو، الله يخليك!
hē, ay shay ḥilu, allāh ykhallīk!
items: do you want to go? (to a man)
to a woman: tabīn trūḥīn? (تبين تروحين؟)
where are you going? (to a group)
to one man: wēn bitrūḥ?; to one woman: wēn bitrūḥīn?
ma abi aṭlaʿ = I don't want to go out
I bring you, I'll get you (to a man)
to a woman: ayīb-lich (أييب لج); tabi ayīb-lak shay? = shall I get you something?

title: Can I help?
goal: Offer to help Maryam at the office and ask her to teach you how she makes a presentation.
tip: agdar (I can) and tigdar (you can) work like abi: the next verb follows with no 'to'. agdar asāʿdak? (can I help you? to a man), agdar asāʿdich? (to a woman). To a woman tigdar becomes tigdarīn: tigdarīn tʿallmīni? (can you teach me?)
grammar: Can + verb: agdar asāʿdak, tigdar, tigdarīn
dialogue: Sure. Can you bring me the papers?
Of course, here you are. What's this?
A presentation for the meeting. Do you want to learn (how)?
Of course. Tomorrow morning, after the meeting.
items: can I help you? (to a man)
to a woman: agdar asāʿdich? (أقدر أساعدج)
you can, can you? (to a man)
can you teach me? (to a man)
to a woman: tigdarīn tʿallmīni? (تقدرين تعلميني؟)
to a woman: tyībīn-li; tigdar tyīb-li…? = can you bring me…?; you'll see written تجيب لي
do you want to learn? (to a man)

title: What do you like?
goal: Tell Saif what you like and don't like about life in Dubai.
tip: aḥibb (I like, I love) takes a noun or a verb with no 'to': aḥibb il-baḥar, aḥibb arūḥ il-baḥar (I like going to the beach). ʿājibni means 'I like it' (it pleases me): ish-shughul ʿājibni. Ask a man ʿājbak? and a woman ʿājbich?
grammar: Like + verb: aḥibb arūḥ, ma aḥibb; ʿājibni
dialogue: How are you? Do you like the job?
زين الحمد لله. إي، عاجبني وايد
zēn il-ḥamdu lillāh. ī, ʿājibni wāyid
Fine, thank God. Yes, I like it a lot.
w shu tḥibb tsawwi yōm is-sabt?
And what do you like doing on Saturdays?
I like going to the beach.
That's fine. I don't like the cold.
items: do you like it?: ʿājbak? (to a man), ʿājbich? (to a woman); for a feminine thing: ʿājbatni (عاجبتني)
what do you do? / what are you doing? (to a man)
it's fine, no big deal, normal

title: Maybe, because…
goal: Answer Saif's invitation to the desert: maybe, why, because, why not.
tip: Give a reason with ʿashān (because) and a whole sentence: ʿashān ʿindi imtiḥān (because I've got an exam). Invitations use tabi + verb: tabi tyī? (do you want to come?). Not sure yet? yimkin (maybe), mub akīd (not sure).
grammar: Want + verb: tabi tyī; because: ʿashān
dialogue: تبي تيي البر ويانا يوم الجمعة؟
tabi tyī l-barr wiyyāna yōm il-jumʿa?
Do you want to come to the desert with us on Friday?
Why? What have you got on?
ʿashān ʿindi imtiḥān, w lāzim adris
Because I've got an exam, and I have to study.
No problem, we'll come back early if you want.
items: do you want to come? (to a man)
to a woman: tabīn tyīn? (تبين تيين؟); you'll see written تجي
also everyday: lann (لأن); fast speech: ʿshān
rāyḥīn il-barr = going out to the desert
culture: In the cooler months, roughly November to March, many Emirati families and friends drive out to il-barr at the weekend to camp, light a fire and drink gahwa. In summer it is far too hot.
